candidate.educational_objective: Apply safe Airborne Precautions PPE doffing, including respirator removal after leaving the room and closing the door.

options.A: Remove the N95 respirator inside the room before touching the gown or gloves, then leave the room and complete the remaining PPE removal in the hallway.
options.B: Keep the N95 on until the end of the shift and remove the gown and gloves after entering another patient-care area, reducing repeated donning and doffing.
options.C: Remove contaminated PPE other than the respirator without self-contamination, clean the hands, exit and close the door, then remove the respirator and perform hand hygiene.
options.D: Leave the room wearing all PPE, remove the respirator first in the hallway, and then return to the isolation area to discard the gown, gloves, and eye protection in the room.

candidate.rationale: CDC core infection-control guidance directs healthcare personnel to remove and discard PPE other than respirators before leaving the patient room or care area. When a respirator is required, it is removed after leaving the room and closing the door, with hand hygiene performed during and after safe doffing according to the facility’s sequence. This avoids the brittle teaching that one universal item must always be removed first while preserving the critical airborne-precaution rule for respirators.
